- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes; apply downward bias to early forecast points.
- After a price spike (e.g., >88.0), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% per day.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices in the 15–20 day horizon; consider mean reversion adjustment by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from forecast for that segment.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust quickly; apply a lag correction by smoothing transition with 1–2 day buffer.
